items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: Why, Harry James' band, with Ernie Andrews, the great singer -- all these guys would come up and play, sit in and jam.

ctx.x: And -- but they had a little pressure from other sources, you know, here in Denver, Colorado. There isn't a day that passes that we go downtown where people say, "Do you ever think the Clef Club they could ever reopen? I've still got my card. We've missed that place." And it was a great place, man, because most of the members were the performers, and this was a place where they would get together and the only time they would have to see each other, you know, and talk -- talk music and get up and perform and one…

And we weren't bothering anybody, weren't breaking any laws, and I just don't understand it. It was a real drag for us because we were known coast to coast on this thing, because when bands would come in town, they'd say, "Hey, where is this (unintelligible) Clef Club club that we've been hearing about, you know, so and so? Well, it doesn't start until 2:00 o'clock in the morning," you know. The guys said, "We'll be there," you know, and all the bands that would play these one nighters that would come in town.…
